justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are represented across EMR Core Service, Billing & Claims Service, and Audit & Compliance Service. However, resource clash checking for scheduling is only generically referenced inside EMR Business Logic Engine without explicit clash detection mechanisms.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-second P95 latency is well supported by Redis Cluster caching, PgBouncer connection pooling, Spring WebFlux asynchronous processing, and Kafka event streaming across services.
justifications.compatibility: Integration Gateway with Apache Camel and FHIR Mapping & Interoperability Component thoroughly fulfills HL7 FHIR API integration for lab, imaging, and clearinghouse external systems.
justifications.usability: The SPA Frontend provides role-based UI routing and views for clinicians, receptionists, billing specialists, and compliance officers, though the patient portal is deferred as a future external system.
justifications.reliability: High availability is supported via Patroni-managed PostgreSQL failover, Redis CRDT active-active replication, Resilience4j circuit breakers, and Strimzi Kafka clusters, though PostgreSQL primary-replica limits true cross-region active-active writes.
justifications.security: Security is thoroughly addressed via Enterprise IdP integration, AES-256 at rest, gRPC over mTLS with eBPF, pgAudit, Ranger ACLs, and AWS S3 Object Lock for HIPAA/GDPR WORM compliance.
justifications.maintainability: Microservices are clearly decoupled by domain with well-defined component responsibilities, Schema Registry for event evolution, and Apache Camel for protocol abstraction.
justifications.portability: Containerized workloads on Kubernetes via Strimzi and Spring Boot deploy smoothly to hybrid on-prem and AWS environments, with minor dependency on AWS S3 Object Lock APIs.

PERF-01.justification: EMR Core Service leverages a dedicated multi-node Redis Cluster for low-latency caching alongside PgBouncer connection pooling, ensuring screen requests resolve sub-second even under concurrent morning rounds load.
sensitivity_points: Redis Cluster cache hit ratio for active clinical records
PgBouncer connection pool sizing under sudden concurrent bursts
tradeoffs: Aggressive caching improves read latency but risks serving stale clinical records

PERF-02.justification: The Integration Gateway receives FHIR payloads and streams them asynchronously via Kafka, decoupling ingestion from synchronous EMR queries and ensuring EMR read latency remains under one second.
sensitivity_points: Kafka consumer throughput and partition parallelism during burst ingestion
Circuit breaker configuration on outbound integration routes
tradeoffs: Asynchronous processing buffers peak load but introduces eventual consistency for lab results

AVAIL-01.justification: While Redis supports active-active CRDT, PostgreSQL relies on standard Patroni primary-replica failover. Multi-site hybrid replication over WAN creates potential replication lag and unaddressed cross-site DNS failover routing mechanisms.
sensitivity_points: PostgreSQL Patroni replication lag across hybrid WAN links
Cross-site traffic rerouting latency between on-prem and cloud
tradeoffs: Synchronous WAN replication increases write latency to guarantee zero data loss

AVAIL-02.justification: Patroni with etcd orchestrates automated PostgreSQL failover within 30 seconds. Resilience4j retries and Kafka event streaming ensure in-flight claims are safely replayed without duplicate submissions.
sensitivity_points: Patroni etcd leader election timeout threshold
Idempotency token enforcement across clearinghouse retry loops
tradeoffs: Fast failover detection thresholds increase risk of false-positive split-brain scenarios

MOD-01.justification: Integration is isolated to the Insurance Clearinghouse Adapter and Camel-based Integration Gateway. Decoupled microservices architecture ensures the EMR Core Service remains completely unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Camel route modularity in the Protocol Translation Engine
Clean boundary between claim scrubbing and external payload mapping
tradeoffs: Dedicated adapter layer increases internal hop latency to gain integration modularity

MOD-02.justification: Modifications are strictly confined to three components: SPA UI Views, EMR Business Logic Engine, and the PostgreSQL schema, with the Audit Interceptor automatically propagating audit event changes.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between EMR relational schema and internal domain transfer objects
Avro/Protobuf schema evolution compatibility rules in Schema Registry
tradeoffs: Strict schema validation prevents runtime errors but requires synchronized multi-component updates

SEC-01.justification: MFA enforcement is delegated to the Enterprise IdP before issuance of tokens. The Audit & Compliance Service's Drools rules engine ingests access events via Kafka to alert on anomalies rapidly.
sensitivity_points: Token cache validation performance in Redis
Drools rule evaluation throughput for real-time security alerts
tradeoffs: Delegating authentication to external IdP adds network hops during login flows

SEC-02.justification: EMR Audit Interceptor and pgAudit capture read access, Drools evaluates access policies for anomalies, and the Retention Manager offloads audit trails to S3 Object Lock for 10-year WORM compliance.
sensitivity_points: Performance overhead of synchronous read audit interception
Correctness of S3 Object Lock compliance retention modes
tradeoffs: Comprehensive read auditing increases persistent storage volume and database write load
